You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (a JavaScript date/time library, Luxon). Your job: find and fix a bug in /luxon/src/interval.js.

Bug report from the user: "There is a bug in `src/interval.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

What this means: Luxon has a global setting `Settings.throwOnInvalid`. When it is true, methods that parse invalid input should throw an `InvalidArgumentError` (or similar) instead of returning an invalid Interval/DateTime. Look at how `Interval.fromISO` in /luxon/src/interval.js handles invalid input and compare with how other classes (e.g. /luxon/src/datetime.js, /luxon/src/duration.js, /luxon/src/info.js) handle `Settings.throwOnInvalid`. Likely `Interval.fromISO` (and possibly related static methods like `Interval.fromDateTimes`, `Interval.after`, `Interval.before`) fails to throw when the setting is enabled, or throws the wrong error type.

Steps:
1. Read /luxon/src/interval.js, /luxon/src/settings.js, /luxon/src/errors.js, and relevant parts of /luxon/src/datetime.js and /luxon/src/duration.js to understand the intended behavior.
2. Check the existing test suite (test/interval/*.js, test/datetime/*.js) for how `throwOnInvalid` is tested elsewhere, e.g. search for `throwOnInvalid` in the repo. Note: there is a test in the repo named `Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid` maybe in test/interval/interval.test.js — check whether it exists and what it expects. Do NOT modify existing tests.
3. Fix the bug in src/interval.js minimally, matching the conventions used elsewhere in the codebase.
4. Verify: run the test suite (e.g. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/interval` or `npm test`) and make sure no previously-passing test breaks. Also write a temporary throwaway script (not committed into the test dir; delete it afterwards) that sets Settings.throwOnInvalid = true and calls Interval.fromISO('invalid') to confirm it throws.

Constraints: do not edit or delete existing tests; do not make unrelated changes; do not add new features. Only fix the bug.

Report back: the exact file/lines changed, the diff, the commands you ran, and the test results (which tests passed/failed before and after).

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library). Your job: find and fix a bug in /luxon/src/duration.js.

Bug report from the user: "There is a bug in `src/duration.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Background: `Duration#normalize()` converts a Duration into a canonical form by rolling smaller units up into larger ones (e.g. 90 minutes -> 1 hour 30 minutes). The hidden test "Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs" presumably iterates over all pairs of units (years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds) and checks that normalizing a duration expressed in one unit yields the expected amount in the larger unit. A likely bug: the conversion matrix / `normalizeUnit` / `shiftTo` / `normalizeValues` logic in src/duration.js (and possibly src/impl/duration.js or the `lowOrderMatrix`/`casualMatrix`/`daysInYear`/`daysInMonth` helpers) mishandles some unit pair (e.g. weeks <-> months, or years <-> months, or days <-> weeks).

Steps:
1. Read /luxon/src/duration.js fully (especially `normalize`, `shiftTo`, `normalizeValues`, `_normalizeUnit`, and the matrices in /luxon/src/impl/duration.js or wherever `lowOrderMatrix`, `casualMatrix`, `daysInYear`, `daysInMonth`, `antiTrivial`, `numberingSystems` live).
2. Read the existing tests: `grep -rn "normalize" /luxon/test/duration` and read test/duration/normalize.test.js (or similar). Do NOT modify existing tests.
3. Work out the mathematically expected conversions from the repository's own documentation/comments (e.g. docs/math.md, the JSDoc on `normalize`/`shiftTo`, and the `conversionAccuracy` matrices). Note the repo's documented convention: in Luxon, a "casual" conversion uses 365 days/year, 30 days/month, 7 days/week, 24 hours/day, etc. Verify each unit pair by hand.
4. Fix the bug minimally in src/duration.js (or the impl file if the bug is there — but the user says src/duration.js).
5. Verify: write a temporary throwaway jest test (inside /luxon, e.g. /luxon/tmp-verify-duration.test.js, DELETE it afterwards) that iterates all unit pairs and checks `Duration.fromObject({[small]: n}).normalize().toObject()` (or `.as(large)`) matches the expected conversion; also run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration` and the full suite `npx jest` to confirm no previously-passing test breaks. Note: there are known pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (ICU French locale) — ignore those, but report them.

Constraints: do not edit or delete existing tests; do not make unrelated changes; do not add new features. Only fix the bug. Do not leave temporary files behind.

Report back: the exact file/lines changed, the diff, the commands you ran, and the test results (which tests passed/failed before and after).

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library).

Task: verify that /luxon/src/duration.js is UNCHANGED relative to the git HEAD commit, and if it is changed, restore it to its original state.

Steps:
1. Run `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` and `git diff -- src/duration.js` and report the output verbatim.
2. If `git diff -- src/duration.js` shows any modification, revert ONLY that file with `cd /luxon && git checkout -- src/duration.js` (do NOT use `git stash`, do NOT touch any other file, do NOT reset the whole repo). Then re-run `git diff -- src/duration.js` to confirm it is empty.
3. Also run `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` again and report the full list of modified files in the working tree (there should be modifications in src/interval.js, src/impl/util.js and/or src/datetime.js from other work — those must be LEFT ALONE).
4. Also check for leftover temporary files created by earlier work: run `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | head -50` and report any untracked files. Delete only obviously temporary scratch files (names like tmp-*.test.js, tmp-probe.js, tmp-verify-*.test.js) at the repo root. Do not delete anything else.

Report: exact commands and their verbatim output, and confirm src/duration.js matches HEAD.

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library). Do NOT change any source file unless a verification below fails; your job is to independently VERIFY an existing fix and report.

A fix was just applied to /luxon/src/interval.js in `Interval.fromISO` (it now wraps the `DateTime.fromISO` calls in try/catch so that `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` doesn't break parsing of `<date>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<date>` intervals, and so invalid input raises `InvalidIntervalError` rather than `InvalidDateTimeError`).

Tasks:
1. Read /luxon/src/interval.js `fromISO` and confirm the logic is correct for these cases (with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`):
   - "2016-01-01/2016-12-31" -> valid Interval
   - "2016-01-01/P1Y" -> valid Interval (end = 2017-01-01)
   - "P1Y/2016-01-01" -> valid Interval (start = 2015-01-01)
   - "foo/bar", "hello", "", null, "P1Y/P1Y", "R5/2008-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M" -> must throw (and the thrown error should be an InvalidIntervalError, i.e. `err.name === 'InvalidIntervalError'` or the message mentions the interval)
   - With `Settings.throwOnInvalid = false` (the default), all the bad inputs must return invalid Intervals with `invalidReason === 'unparsable'` and NOT throw.
   - Also check `Interval.fromISO("2016-01-01/P1Y", { zone: "Europe/Paris" })` works with throwOnInvalid true and false.
2. Write a temporary jest test file OUTSIDE the repo's test dir (e.g. /tmp/verify-interval.test.js) or a temporary script you delete afterwards. The repo uses babel/jest; the simplest approach is to create a temp test file inside /luxon (e.g. /luxon/tmp-verify-interval.test.js) with `import { Interval, Settings } from "./src/luxon"`, run `cd /luxon && npx jest tmp-verify-interval.test.js`, then DELETE the file. Do not leave any new files behind. Do NOT modify any existing test file.
3. Run `cd /luxon && npx jest` (full suite) and report the exact list of failing tests and suites. Note: there are known pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js related to ICU French locale formatting — confirm whether the only failures are those.
4. Report: the exact commands run, the observed results for each case above, the full-suite failure list, and whether the fix is correct or needs adjustment. If it needs adjustment, describe precisely what and why, but prefer NOT to edit unless clearly broken.

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library).

Task: revert the changes made to /luxon/src/interval.js so that it matches the original git HEAD version exactly.

Steps:
1. `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` and `git diff -- src/interval.js` — report verbatim.
2. Run `cd /luxon && git checkout -- src/interval.js` (revert ONLY this one file; do NOT touch src/impl/util.js, src/datetime.js, src/duration.js, or any test file; do NOT run git stash/reset/clean).
3. Confirm with `cd /luxon && git diff -- src/interval.js` (must be empty) and `git hash-object src/interval.js` vs `git rev-parse HEAD:src/interval.js` (must be identical).
4. Confirm `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` shows src/interval.js no longer modified, and report which other files are modified (leave them alone).
5. Also delete any leftover scratch files at the repo root matching `tmp-*` (e.g. tmp-probe.js, tmp-probe-dst.js, tmp-verify-*.test.js) that are untracked — but do NOT delete anything else, and do not delete files inside test/.

Report: exact commands and verbatim output, and confirm src/interval.js is byte-identical to HEAD.

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library). Your job: find and fix a bug in /luxon/src/datetime.js.

Bug report from the user: "There is a bug in `src/datetime.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Background: In 1974 the USA enacted year-round Daylight Saving Time (Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act) — DST began January 6, 1974 and ended October 27, 1974. Luxon's `DateTime#isInDST()` (and the related `isOffsetFixed` / `isInDST` logic) compares the DateTime's offset with the offset in January and May of the same year. Look at the implementation of `isInDST()` in /luxon/src/datetime.js and figure out why it fails for dates between Jan 6 and Oct 27, 1974 in the America/New_York zone (or generally in zones with unusual DST rules).

Steps:
1. Read the `isInDST` implementation and surrounding code in /luxon/src/datetime.js. Also read /luxon/src/zone.js and /luxon/src/zones/*.js for the offset APIs available.
2. Search the tests for `isInDST` (`grep -rn "isInDST" /luxon/test`) to see the existing expectations. Do NOT modify existing tests.
3. Determine the correct expected behaviour from the repository's own docs/comments/tests and from the universally-accepted meaning of "is in DST".
4. Fix the bug minimally in src/datetime.js.
5. Verify with a temporary throwaway script (delete it afterwards) that runs with TZ=America/New_York, e.g. `TZ=America/New_York node -e "..."` using the source (you may need babel; check /luxon/package.json and jest config — easiest is to add a temporary jest test file in a scratch location outside the repo test dir, or use `npx jest` with a temp test file that you delete afterwards; do NOT leave any new test files in the repo). Check `DateTime.fromISO('1974-06-01', {zone: 'America/New_York'}).isInDST()` is true and that dates outside Jan 6–Oct 27 1974 are false, and that normal years (e.g. 2017) still behave correctly.
6. Run the full test suite `cd /luxon && npx jest` and confirm no previously-passing test breaks.

Constraints: do not edit or delete existing tests; do not make unrelated changes; do not add new features. Only fix the bug.

Report back: the exact file/lines changed, the diff, the commands you ran, and the test results (which tests passed/failed before and after).

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library). Your job: find and fix a bug in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js.

Bug report from the user: "There is a bug in `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js`. Once it is fixed, the tests `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid` and `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset` should pass; the versions of them that check this are not in the repository, so their names only describe the expected behaviour."

Background: `FixedOffsetZone.instance(offset)` returns a singleton for a numeric offset; `FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier(specifier)` parses strings like "UTC+6" / "UTC-3:30". When given a non-numeric offset (e.g. `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")` or `parseSpecifier("blorp")`), the zone should be invalid (e.g. `zone.isValid === false`), and a DateTime created in that zone should itself be invalid. Currently the code probably returns a zone with a NaN offset, or a valid zone, so the DateTime ends up valid (or throws).

Steps:
1. Read /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js, /luxon/src/zone.js, /luxon/src/zones/invalidZone.js, /luxon/src/settings.js and the parts of /luxon/src/datetime.js that construct a zone from an options object (`normalizeZone`, `DateTime.fromObject`, `DateTime.local`, `friendlyDateTime`).
2. Search the tests: `grep -rn "FixedOffsetZone\|fixedOffset" /luxon/test` and read test/zones/fixedOffsetZone.test.js (if it exists) and test/zones/zone.test.js. Do NOT modify existing tests. Note that the two hidden tests named in the bug report may not exist in the repo — that's expected.
3. Determine the expected behaviour from the repository's own docs/comments/tests (e.g. `Zone#isValid`, `InvalidZone`, and how `DateTime` handles an invalid zone — look at how `DateTime.fromObject` / `normalizeZone` / `parseDataToDateTime` react to a zone whose `isValid` is false).
4. Fix the bug minimally in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js (and only there unless the bug cannot be fixed there — if you believe another file must change, explain why in your report before changing it).
5. Verify with a temporary throwaway jest test file inside /luxon (e.g. /luxon/tmp-verify-foz.test.js, DELETE it afterwards) that checks:
   - `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp").isValid === false`
   - `FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier("blorp").isValid === false` (and that `parseSpecifier("UTC+6")` still works, offset 360)
   - `DateTime.fromObject({ year: 2017, month: 5, day: 25 }, { zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp") }).isValid === false` (and does not throw)
   - normal cases still work: `FixedOffsetZone.instance(60).offset(...) === 60`, `DateTime.fromISO("2017-05-25", { zone: "UTC+6" })` valid with the right offset.
   Then run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/zones` and the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest`. Note: there are known pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (ICU French locale, 2 tests) — ignore those but report them.
6. Delete all temporary files you create.

IMPORTANT COORDINATION NOTE: other agents are concurrently editing /luxon/src/datetime.js and /luxon/src/impl/util.js. Do NOT edit those files, and do not revert or 'clean up' code you did not write. Only touch src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js.

Constraints: do not edit or delete existing tests; do not make unrelated changes; do not add new features. Only fix the bug.

Report back: the exact file/lines changed, the diff, the commands you ran, and the test results (which tests passed/failed before and after).

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library). Your job: find and fix a bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js.

Bug report from the user: "There is a bug in `src/impl/util.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#toISODate() correctly pads negative years` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Background: Luxon's `DateTime#toISODate()` (and `toISO()`, `toISOTime()`) formats dates as ISO 8601. For years outside 0-9999 the ISO representation uses an expanded year format with a sign and at least 6 digits, e.g. year -100 -> "-000100-01-01", year 10000 -> "+010000-01-01". Look at /luxon/src/datetime.js `toISODate`/`toISO` and the helper functions in /luxon/src/impl/util.js (e.g. `padStart`, `untruncateYear`, `signedOffset`, `objToLocalTS`) that build the year string. A likely bug is that negative years are not padded correctly (e.g. `-100` -> "-100-01-01" instead of "-000100-01-01"), or the padding helper mishandles the sign.

IMPORTANT COORDINATION NOTE: another agent may be concurrently editing /luxon/src/impl/util.js to fix a different bug (leap-year/February handling around the year-100 barrier). To avoid clobbering their work: (a) read the file immediately before editing, (b) make the smallest possible targeted edit (do not rewrite whole functions or reformat the file), (c) after editing, re-read the file and confirm the rest of it is intact, (d) never revert or 'clean up' code you did not write.

Steps:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js and the ISO-output code in /luxon/src/datetime.js (`toISO`, `toISODate`, `toISOTime`, `toISOWeekDate`).
2. Search tests: `grep -rn "toISODate\|negative year\|untruncateYear\|padStart" /luxon/test /luxon/src`. Do NOT modify existing tests.
3. Determine the expected behaviour from the repo's own docs/comments and from ISO 8601 (expanded years: sign + at least 4 digits, and Luxon's own convention as evidenced by existing tests/comments).
4. Fix the bug minimally.
5. Verify with a temporary throwaway jest test file inside /luxon (e.g. /luxon/tmp-verify-iso.test.js, DELETE it afterwards) that checks e.g. `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -100, month: 1, day: 1 }).toISODate()` and `.toISO()` produce correctly padded negative years, plus a few positive/zero cases (year 0, 1, 99, 999, 1000, 10000). Then run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime` and the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest`. Note: there are known pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (ICU French locale, 2 tests) — ignore those but report them.
6. Delete all temporary files you create. Do not leave scratch files behind.

Constraints: do not edit or delete existing tests; do not make unrelated changes; do not add new features. Only fix the bug.

Report back: the exact file/lines changed, the diff, the commands you ran, and the test results (which tests passed/failed before and after).

You are working in a Linux container. The repository is checked out at /luxon (Luxon, a JavaScript date/time library). Your job: find and fix a bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js.

Bug report from the user: "There is a bug in `src/impl/util.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Background: Luxon's DateTime#plus adds durations. There is a known class of bugs around years before 100 AD (the "100 barrier"), because JavaScript's `Date` constructor maps years 0-99 to 1900-1999. Luxon handles this in src/impl/util.js (look for helpers like `isLeapYear`, `daysInMonth`, `daysInYear`, `weeksInWeekYear`, `untruncateYear`, `padStart`, `parseInteger`, `parseMillis`, `parseFloating`, `roundTo`, `floorMod`, `objToLocalTS`, `signedOffset`, `isUndefined`, `isNumber`, `normalizeObject`, `asNumber`, `integerBetween`, `bestBy`, `pick`, `hasOwnProperty`, `validateWeekSettings`, etc.). A likely culprit is `daysInMonth` or `isLeapYear` or `objToLocalTS` handling of leap years / February for years < 100.

Steps:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js fully, plus /luxon/src/datetime.js (especially the `plus`/`minus`/`set`/`objToLocalTS` code paths) and /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js.
2. Look at the existing tests: search the test directory for "100 barrier" or similar tests (e.g. `grep -rn "barrier" /luxon/test`). Do NOT modify existing tests. Also check git log/history is NOT allowed to be used to find the future fix — only read the current source.
3. Determine the correct expected behaviour from the repository itself (docstrings, comments, existing tests, mathematical expectations about leap years: a year is a leap year if divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400; year 0 and negative years should be handled correctly).
4. Fix the bug minimally in src/impl/util.js.
5. Verify: run the relevant tests, e.g. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime` and `npx jest test/impl`, plus the full suite `npx jest` if time permits. Make sure no previously-passing test breaks. Also write a temporary throwaway script (delete it afterwards) that exercises DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 1, day: 31}).plus({months: 1}) and similar cases spanning February across the year-100 barrier, and confirm the results are correct.

Constraints: do not edit or delete existing tests; do not make unrelated changes; do not add new features. Only fix the bug.

Report back: the exact file/lines changed, the diff, the commands you ran, and the test results (which tests passed/failed before and after).
